content.title: ​​Kelly Ripa Tears Up Paying Tribute to Husband Mark Consuelos' Dad After His Death: 'He Was the Greatest Person'
content.text: NEED TO KNOW Mark Consuelos announced on Monday, April 6, that his father, Saul Consuelos, died last month after a long illnessWhile reflecting on their memories with him, Kelly Ripa, who has been married to Mark for nearly 30 years, got emotionalShe went on to praise Saul's impact on her life and the lives of the three children she and Mark share Kelly Ripa and Mark Consuelos are mourning the loss of his father. On the Monday, April 6 episode of Live with Kelly and Mark, the couple, who have been married for nearly three decades, announced that Mark’s dad, Saul Consuelos, died two weeks prior “after a long bout with illness.” Ripa, 55, got emotional while reflecting on Saul, telling Mark, also 55, that they “have been blessed.” “You have been blessed more because you knew him your whole life,” she said. “I only got to know my father-in-law for 31 years, but they were the best 31 years of my life. I can honestly say that I will miss him every day for the rest of my life, as I know you will, as our children will. He was the greatest person I've ever known, and he really is so symbolic of everything you are.” Calling Saul “a fantastic man,” Mark said all of his own “good” qualities came from his dad. “It's funny, I used to make a joke about my dad: If you asked him what time it was he would tell you how to build a watch,” the host quipped. “There was a lot of lectures, and I learned so much. If he was fixing something in the house, he'd make me watch him do it. And I didn't know at the time why he was doing that, because now at the house I'm able to at least do half the stuff that he does.” “I do everything the way he did it,” Mark added. Related Stories Saul was born in Mexico and immigrated to the United States in his early teens. He went on to join the military, serving for 30 years. “This young kid from Mexico just got his education through the Navy, was always going to school. Brilliant,” Mark continued. “Got his Master's while I was a kid. He loved this country so much. He really loved this country so much. He really is, I would say, an example, if you were to put a face to an immigrant, he would be the prime example of what this country promises people here in this country.” Mark is one of three children, who Ripa said are all “extraordinary,” and his primary goal now is to take care of his mother, Camilla. “We're trying to convince my mom to move to New York. She's such a character. She's very stubborn,” Mark said. Mark Consuelos and his father Saul Consuelos. Ripa then shared her favorite memories of Saul, whom she praised for playing such a big role in the lives of the three children she and Mark share: Michael, 28, Lola, 24, and Joaquin, 23. “I'm so grateful to your dad for everything he did for me,” she said. “A lot of times you'd be away working and we would take the show on the road and your dad would come to take care of the kids so that I could go to work.” She continued: “I keep explaining to my kids how lucky they were to be adults, to have had their [grandparents]. They still have three grandparents, and they took it particularly hard. This is their first loss that they've ever experienced in their lives. By the time I was 8, I had no grandparents, and you got to grow up with [them]. You got to have deep meaningful conversations.” Saul even stepped in as a father figure when Mark was out of town for work, leading to some hilarious confusion among other parents at the kids’ school, Ripa remembered. “There was a long period of time where people thought that my father-in-law was my husband on back-to-school night, because he was always with me,” she said. “He was very involved with the curriculum of the school and he wanted to know things.” One year, Ripa joked that Mark attended a school event with her instead of Saul, and people thought she had remarried. “They were like, ‘Is this your new husband?'” Ripa said with a laugh. “‘’Cause he resembles your old husband.’ And I was like, ‘No, this is my husband. That was my father-in-law.’ But everybody assumed for a long time that my father-in-law was my husband. Because in New York, it's not unusual.”
